overview_markdown:
TitanClaw is a Rust-based, security-first reimplementation of OpenClaw/IronClaw aimed at users who want real automation rather than just chat. It emphasizes data control, hardened sandboxing, and high-throughput orchestration, with multi-provider inference support including NEAR AI, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, and Tinfoil, plus automatic provider failover.

Architecturally, it ships a scheduler with parallel jobs, a Docker worker/orchestrator flow, a WASM-based dynamic tool system, and streaming via SSE/WebSocket with live shell output and piped execution. Advanced tracks include tree-sitter AST context indexing with a queryable memory graph, a deterministic reflex fast-path that routes recurring prompts to compiled tools, and a distributed swarm mesh where scheduler subtasks offload to capability-matching peers with deterministic local fallback.

Compared to OpenClaw, TitanClaw trades ecosystem breadth for a smaller, hardened Rust core: recent releases added CLI parity features (cron, channels, backup, browser, approvals, agents, canvas), runtime reliability hardening, and OAuth state verification for WASM callbacks. It is a promising pick for security-conscious self-hosters, but its 25-star community and emerging plugin ecosystem mean it lacks OpenClaw's maturity and support network.
